audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph monthly military divisions, tribal leaders, royal property managers, counselors, and commanders, first-pass restored draft; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for rotating military system, under-twenty exclusion, unfinished census and wrath, tribal representation, royal agricultural wealth, migrant/foreign managers, animal labor, counselor networks, Ahithophel context, nepotism, and public-private boundaries.

verses.restored: Children of Israel by number—ancestral heads, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and officers serving king in every matter of divisions—came in and went out month by month through all months; each division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Over first division for first month was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
He was from sons of Perez and chief of all army commanders for first month.
Over division of second month was Dodai the Ahohite, and Mikloth was leader; in division were twenty-four thousand.
Third army commander for third month was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, chief; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
This Benaiah was mighty among thirty and over thirty; Ammizabad his son was over his division.
Fourth for fourth month was Asahel brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; in division were twenty-four thousand.
Fifth for fifth month was Shamhuth the Izrahite; in division were twenty-four thousand.
Sixth for sixth month was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; in division were twenty-four thousand.
Seventh for seventh month was Helez the Pelonite from Ephraim; in division were twenty-four thousand.
Eighth for eighth month was Sibbecai the Hushathite from Zerahites; in division were twenty-four thousand.
Ninth for ninth month was Abiezer the Anathothite from Benjaminites; in division were twenty-four thousand.
Tenth for tenth month was Maharai the Netophathite from Zerahites; in division were twenty-four thousand.
Eleventh for eleventh month was Benaiah the Pirathonite from Ephraim; in division were twenty-four thousand.
Twelfth for twelfth month was Heldai the Netophathite from Othniel; in division were twenty-four thousand.
Over tribes of Israel: for Reuben, Eliezer son of Zichri; for Simeon, Shephatiah son of Maacah;
for Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
for Judah, Elihu from brothers of David; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael;
for Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;
for Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for half-tribe Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;
for half-Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;
for Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were leaders of tribes of Israel.
David did not take number of those twenty years old and under, because YHWH had said Israel would be multiplied like stars of heavens.
Joab son of Zeruiah began to count but did not finish; wrath came upon Israel because of this, and number did not enter account in chronicles of king David.
Over king's treasuries was Azmaveth son of Adiel; over storehouses in fields, cities, villages, and towers was Jonathan son of Uzziah.
Over field workers cultivating ground was Ezri son of Chelub.
Over vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite; over vineyard produce for wine stores was Zabdi the Shiphmite.
Over olive and sycamore trees in Shephelah was Baal-hanan the Gederite; over oil stores was Joash.
Over herds grazing in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite; over herds in valleys was Shaphat son of Adlai.
Over camels was Obil the Ishmaelite; over donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite.
Over flocks was Jaziz the Hagarite. All these were officials over king David's property.
Jonathan David's uncle was counselor, understanding and scribe; Jehiel son of Hachmoni was with king's sons.
Ahithophel was king's counselor; Hushai the Archite was king's companion.
After Ahithophel were Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar; Joab was commander of king's army.

translation_notes: Twelve rotating divisions create a permanent military system affecting soldiers, families, farms, and local economies even outside active war.
Excluding those twenty and under from the census is a meaningful limit, but the remaining system still raises conscription and consent concerns.
The unfinished census recalls chapter 21, showing that administrative counting and militarized control remain unresolved rather than inherently forbidden.
Tribal leaders do not guarantee full representation of women, poor people, local communities, or dissenters.
Royal property encompasses treasuries, storehouses, fields, vineyards, orchards, wine, oil, herds, camels, donkeys, and flocks, revealing a vast extraction and management system.
Farmers and animal keepers generate royal wealth; they require recognition, fair conditions, and protection from exploitation.
Obil the Ishmaelite and Jaziz the Hagarite hold trusted roles, undermining ethnic-purity narratives.
Animals are living beings cared for by workers, not merely royal inventory.
Ahithophel's later suicide in 2 Samuel 17 must remain visible; his name is not simply a neutral office-holder entry.
Family and companion appointments raise questions about nepotism and blurred public-private power.
safety_note: Do not glorify permanent militarization, conscription, royal extraction, nepotism, or ownership of workers and animals. Center underage protection, farmers, migrant managers, animal care, public accountability, and families carrying the hidden cost of rotating armies.
